headline: Persian Gulf Region: Iran war live: Explosion rocks Sanaa; missiles intercepted over Riyadh
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- Persian Gulf Region: Iran war live: Explosion rocks Sanaa; missiles intercepted over Riyadh.
- Western Russia: One Killed in Samara Region as Ukraine Strikes Oil Refinery.
- Africa: Iran warns of destructive response if key facilities are attacked.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Estimates of Russians killed in Ukraine surpass all combined US war deaths since WWI.
- Military Times, 8 hours ago: Estimates of Russians killed in Ukraine surpass all combined US war deaths since WWI.
More than 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the war in Ukraine since Russia launched its full-scale war against the nation nearly five years ago.
- Military Times, 9 hours ago: All USS George Washington CSG sailors returning from deployment to be provided ashore accommodations.
Sailors from the USS George Washington carrier strike group will be able to sleep in off-ship beds when they return from their roughly six-month deployment, the Navy said.
The Caribbean - bottom line: ODPEM fiasco could scare off future donors, PNP warns.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 2 days ago: ODPEM fiasco could scare off future donors, PNP warns.
Local and international partners could become reluctant to donate to Jamaica in future national emergencies if confidence in the management of humanitarian aid is not urgently restored, Opposition Spokesperson on Local Government Natalie Neita Garvey has warned. This comes amid findings from a report by the auditor general that the Office of Disaster Preparedness and Emergency Management (ODPEM) misused funds donated for a Government-directed roof programme to clear third-party goods.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America - bottom line: Argentina officially enters a technical recession.
- Buenos Aires Herald, one day ago: Argentina officially enters a technical recession.
Despite September's month-over-month growth, poor figures for July and August dragged down quarterly performance. Economists are already warning of “stagflation” La entrada Argentina officially enters a technical recession se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald.

EUROPE

- The Moscow Times, 17 hours ago: One Killed in Samara Region as Ukraine Strikes Oil Refinery.
Independent media reported that fires broke out at two Rosneft-operated oil refineries in the southern Samara region following overnight attacks.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 12 hours ago: Ukrainian forces thwart Russian assault south of Dobropillia – video.
25th Sicheslav Airborne Brigade has reported that Russian forces attempting to advance south of Dobropillia under cover of strong winds were stopped after FPV drone strikes and a minefield disabled their armoured vehicles.
- The Moscow Times, 10 hours ago: Russian Official Warns of Ukrainian Drone Attacks on Utility Infrastructure This Winter.
The comments mirrored warnings from Ukrainian leaders about the risk of winter attacks on energy infrastructure disrupting power and heating supplies.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 10 hours ago: Russian drone attacks car in Kharkiv Oblast, killing two.
A Russian drone struck a civilian car in Kharkiv Oblast's Zolochiv hromada on 25 November, killing two people, likely a local couple, Syniehubov said.
Southern Europe - bottom line: French presidential hopeful Teddy Riner says Ukraine is ‘not our war’.
- Politico Europe, 10 hours ago: French presidential hopeful Teddy Riner says Ukraine is ‘not our war’.
The Olympic gold medalist's remarks on Russia's ongoing full-scale invasion provoked a backlash.

Residents of the Borgu district in central Nigeria were left grappling with the aftermath of deadly communal attacks on Tuesday. Assaults killed several dozens in the area during the weekend.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 22 hours ago: Sudan: Violations Against Women, Girls Escalates.
[Dabanga] Blue Nile State -- The Strategic Initiative for Women in the Horn of Africa (SIHA Network) has reported the abduction of 28 women and girls fleeing fighting in Damazin and 15 cases of conflict-related sexual violence against girls under the age of 18 in Blue Nile state. In a statement published yesterday, the organisation has warned of escalating violations against women and girls as fighting intensifies, with thousands of families fleeing their homes and facing growing humanitarian risks.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 14 hours ago: Uganda: Uganda, Somalia Agree to Intensify Military Offensive Against Al-Shabaab.
[Independent (Kampala)] Kampala -- Uganda and Somalia have agreed to intensify military operations against Al-Shabaab militants and explore alternative funding mechanisms to sustain security operations in Somalia. The agreement was reached during a meeting between President Yoweri Museveni and his Somali counterpart, Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, who was on a one-day official visit to Uganda on November 23, 2026.

- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 16 hours ago: South Africa: How to Survive Black Friday Without Going Broke.
[Scrolla] Old Mutual financial education head John Manyike warns shoppers against buying things they do not need simply because they are on sale. Shoppers are urged to watch out for fake online sellers, check expiry dates and keep enough money aside for December and January expenses.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 16 hours ago: Zimbabwe: Zimbabwe Women's Cricket Coach Mark Coles Fined for Abusive Language Towards Ireland Captain.
[New Zimbabwe] ZIMBABWE women's head coach Mark Coles has been fined 65% of his match fees and handed three demerit points after admitting to two breaches of the International Cricket Council (ICC) Code of Conduct.

A special MP/MLA court in Rouse Avenue cancelled a non-bailable warrant against businessman Dinesh Pandey. The Enforcement Directorate is surprised and plans to appeal this decision in the Delhi high court. Pandey is reportedly involved in transferring Rs 10.4 crore through a shell company to Associated Journals Ltd. The court criticized the investigating officer for using a sealed cover, which is typically standard practice.

- Times of India - Top Stories, 11 hours ago: Missouri HOA demands 5 neighbours' consent for 12 solar panels; court nixes fees.
In a significant ruling, a Missouri couple clashed with their homeowners association over the installation of solar panels. The court decided that the HOA improperly sought legal fees, affirming that no property rules were breached. This case highlighted Missouri's solar energy legislation, which fortifies homeowners' rights to adopt renewable energy solutions. Ultimately, the appeals court reversed a previous ruling that had favored the homeowners association.

But for Hondurans, the message is less stark. “Overall, Gracias a Dios is a low-crime, functioning department,” says a State Department background report. Hong Kong’s Pakistani community is mourning the loss of self-made businessman Javaid Mehmood, who was killed in a Tsim Sha Tsui drink-driving crash, with a longtime friend remembering him as a quiet philanthropist who took pride in putting students through school. Mehmood, 53, died and three other people were injured after a car ploughed into pedestrians on Prat Avenue on Sunday afternoon. Australia - bottom line: Kurtley Beale back in Wallabies team for first time in five years.
- ABC News Australia, just now: Kurtley Beale back in Wallabies team for first time in five years.
The return of Kurtley Beale to the Wallabies team for cap number 96 after a five-year absence is a reward for his continuing excellence, coach Les Kiss insists.

An eastern blue groper estimated to be more than 30 years old has gone missing from its habit in Mollymook, days after being discovered with injuries from a suspected speargun attack.

David Warner has delivered further barbs on social media amid the sandpaper scandal, accusing journalists of perpetuating speculation instead of finding facts.
